result:
I saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. Run on Q2, the same script reproduces all 10 reference values exactly.

| Item | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | smb, 336,387,554 |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 247 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | hw, 306,694,527 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-08 |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | u168@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 229 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 686,876 |
| h. September vs. August growth | -8.7% |

The Q2 reference values only came out right after three adjustments to the raw data:
- **Dates use Korean time (KST, UTC+9).** Order times are stored in UTC. Filtering in UTC gave different Q2 numbers (for example, the top month came out as June instead of May). After shifting to KST, everything matched.
- **One customer = one email.** The `customers` table has 300 rows but only 250 distinct emails. I treated rows with the same email, ignoring case and spaces, as one customer. This affects b, e and f.
- **Segment and category labels are cleaned up.** Values like "SMB", " consumer" and "Enterprise " were trimmed and lowercased.

Refunds for the same order line were summed.

STATUS: DONE
